title: LSASS memory credential dumping via hidden PowerShell on scranton
rationale: All these findings describe the same attacker action: a hidden, obfuscated PowerShell process (PID 2976, spawned by control.exe, user pbeesly) on scranton.dmevals.local opening lsass.exe with full-access masks (0x1f3fff, 0x1fffff) and 'Read from process memory' (Security 4663), plus the same primitive via wsmprovhost.exe on nashua. This is credential dumping from LSASS memory, best fitting T1003.001 (LSASS Memory).

title: Plaintext credentials in PsExec command lines for lateral movement to NASHUA
rationale: Both findings describe the same action: PsExec64.exe invoked four times from scranton with the cleartext password 'Fl0nk3rt0n!T0by' for dmevals\pbeesly on \\NASHUA, launching C:\Windows\Temp\python.exe. Credentials exposed in process command lines fit T1552.001 (Credentials In Files).

title: Hardcoded WebDAV exfil credentials in Invoke-Exfil script
rationale: The Invoke-Exfil PowerShell script (psversion.ps1) compresses the Downloads folder to OfficeSupplies.7z and copies it to a WebDAV share using hardcoded plaintext credentials ('cozy' / 'MyCozyPassw0rd!'). Hardcoded credentials in a script fit T1552.001 (Credentials In Files).

title: Get-PrivateKeys exports LocalMachine certificate private keys to .pfx on scranton
rationale: These findings all describe the same action: the PowerShell function Get-PrivateKeys (from C:\Program Files\SysinternalsSuite\readme.ps1) enumerating cert:\LocalMachine and exporting every certificate with its private key to password-protected .pfx files (e.g. coyn5igj.3io.pfx) in the user's Downloads folder. This is theft of private keys, best fitting T1552.004 (Private Keys).

title: Python relay/listener tooling on nashua with NTLM network logon
rationale: C:\Windows\Temp\python.exe launched by PSEXESVC.exe making 348 outbound TCP connections to 192.168.0.4:8443, with SMB/NBT-NS traffic and an NTLM network logon, is consistent with SMB relay/name-resolution poisoning, best fitting T1557.001 (Name Resolution Poisoning and SMB Relay).

title: Single responder MAC for most Zeek connections (possible L2 redirection)
rationale: A single responder MAC answering for most Zeek connections could reflect ARP cache poisoning, but the MAC is a synthetic placeholder and no corroborating evidence exists; best fit is T1557.002 (ARP Cache Poisoning), assessed suspicious/low confidence.

title: csc.exe compiles attacker DLLs from PowerShell on scranton
rationale: powershell.exe invoking csc.exe to compile attacker source into DLLs is on-host payload compilation, not credential access; best ATT&CK fit is T1027 (Obfuscated Files or Information).

title: Python interpreter dropped in Temp and launched via PsExec on nashua
rationale: C:\Windows\Temp\python.exe launched by PSEXESVC.exe is attacker tool execution, not credential access; best ATT&CK fit is T1059 (Command and Scripting Interpreter).

title: accesschk.exe permission reconnaissance on scranton
rationale: Sysinternals accesschk.exe launched by powershell.exe is permission reconnaissance, not credential access; best ATT&CK fit is T1069 (Permission Groups Discovery).

title: SDelete anti-forensics wiping of payload and staged archives on scranton
rationale: sdelete64.exe securely wiping the .scr payload, Draft.Zip and SysinternalsSuite.zip is indicator removal/anti-forensics, not credential access; best ATT&CK fit is T1070 (Indicator Removal).

title: Malicious .scr payload in ProgramData launched by explorer on scranton
rationale: A .scr executable in C:\ProgramData\victim launched by explorer.exe is user execution of a malicious file, not credential access; best ATT&CK fit is T1204 (User Execution).

title: hostui.exe LOLbin launched by PowerShell on scranton
rationale: hostui.exe launched by powershell.exe is abuse of a legitimate signed binary as a LOLbin, not credential access; best ATT&CK fit is T1218 (System Binary Proxy Execution).

title: sdclt.exe LOLbin launched by cmd.exe on scranton
rationale: sdclt.exe launched by cmd.exe and spawning control.exe is LOLbin abuse, not credential access; best ATT&CK fit is T1218 (System Binary Proxy Execution).

title: Rar.exe password-protected staging and sdelete wiping on nashua
rationale: Rar.exe creating a password-protected archive of collected data and sdelete64.exe wiping it is collection/archive staging and anti-forensics, not credential access; best ATT&CK fit is T1560 (Archive Collected Data).
